source.publication: 2025 Nebraska Individual Income Tax and Amended Return Booklet (8-307-2025), with 2025 Form 1040N and Schedule I
source.section: Form 1040N PDF pages 1-2, lines 2a, 4a, 4b, 4, 5, 6, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 34, 35; booklet PDF page 12 lines 2a, 4a, 4b; PDF page 13 line 5, line 6 and the Nebraska Standard Deduction Chart; PDF page 14 lines 10 to 18; PDF page 17 lines 34, 35 and the Federal Tax Liability Worksheet; PDF pages 46-49 Tax Table and over-77,760 worksheet (schedule as numbers, as settled in the record from the table); Schedule I line 31; booklet PDF page 26 Line 31; record ne_social_security_exclusion

worked: Single, 70: Social Security 30,000 and private pension 30,050. Federal taxable Social Security: provisional income 30,050.00 + 15,000.00 = 45,050.00; 85% x (45,050.00 - 34,000.00) = 9,392.50 + 4,500.00 = 13,892.50, under the 85% limit of 25,500.00. All of the taxable part comes out on Schedule I line 31, at any income: the booklet says there is no longer a federal AGI threshold. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (you) 30,050.00 + taxable Social Security 13,892.50 = 43,942.50. Federal taxable income = 43,942.50 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 for 65 or older = 26,192.50 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 1040N filing status (1) single, resident. Line 2a: 1 box(es) checked: box 1 (you born 1955-07-17, before January 2, 1961). Line 4a 1; line 4c none; line 4 total 1. Line 5 federal AGI 43,942.50. Line 6 Nebraska standard deduction, chart for 1 box(es): 10,600.00 (0-box amount 8,600.00 plus 1 x 2,000.00, the step between chart rows); lines 7 to 9 skipped (no federal itemizing); line 10 10,600.00. Line 11 = 43,942.50 - 10,600.00 = 33,342.50. Line 12 adjustments increasing federal AGI 0.00. Schedule I Part B: line 31 Social Security included in federal AGI 13,892.50; line 44 total 13,892.50. Line 13 = 13,892.50. Line 14 Nebraska taxable income = 33,342.50 + 0.00 - 13,892.50 = 19,450.00. State income after additions and subtractions (before the deduction) = 43,942.50 + 0.00 - 13,892.50 = 30,050.00. Line 15 tax, schedule as numbers (single column): 2.46% x 4,030.00 = 99.138 + 3.51% x 15,420.00 = 541.242; total 640.380, rounded once to 640.38. The Tax Table row 19,360 to 19,460 gives 639; expected keeps the schedule. Line 16 0.00 (no lump-sum or early-distribution tax); line 17 = 640.38. Line 18 personal exemption credit = 171 x 1 = 171.00; line 34 171.00. Line 35 = 640.38 - 171.00 = 469.38. Federal Tax Liability Worksheet (PDF page 17): net adjustments -13,892.50 are under 5,000, but it does not reduce line 35: the federal tax before credits is at least 10% x 26,192.50 = 2,619.25, above worksheet line 2 of 469.38.
accepted_approximations: The brackets are fitted to the printed tax table; no rate schedule is in the sources. The start of the 5.20% band is not pinned by the table: single and married filing separately 38,793 to 38,897, head of household 57,535 to 57,639, married filing jointly 77,501 to 77,760. The table's rows also round to the dollar at the row's midpoint, and the bands do neither.
